abertura: Your interlocutor is a lawyer from another country. She is competent and she knows nothing about how your system works.
Mark the two things she needs before your argument can land.

itens.t: Who decides, and what exactly they decide.
itens.porque: Yes. Without it she maps your case onto her own system and hears a different argument from the one you are making.

itens.t: The full history of the institution.
itens.porque: No. It is the kind of context that feels responsible and costs you the whole three minutes.

itens.t: That the defence is a public body, not a firm the family hired.
itens.porque: Yes. It changes what she assumes about choice, strategy and resources.

itens.t: How many cases you handle in a year.
itens.porque: No — it is about you, not about what she has to understand to follow the case.

itens.t: The name of the court where it happened.
itens.porque: No. A name she cannot place adds nothing she can use.

sec1.rationale: She needs whatever changes the meaning of what you are about to say. Everything else is background, and background spends the three minutes you have.

nota.titulo: The test for what to explain
nota.texto:
Not “is it interesting?” but does my argument mean something different if she does not know it?

If the defence being a public body changes how she hears your position — and it does — it goes in. If the name of the court does not, it stays out. Three minutes is short, and background is what eats it.

nota.titulo: “Which means that” is the one that does the explaining
nota.texto:
Explaining a system to an outsider is not a list of facts — it is a chain of consequences. In our system the defence is a public body, which means that the family does not choose us, which means that…

Without it you produce facts and she has to assemble them herself, in a language that is not hers either.

sec3.titulo: In or out of three minutes
abertura: Six things you could say to her. Decide what each one is for.
opcoes: she needs it or the argument changes meaning
interesting, and it costs you time
it belongs later, if she asks

itens.t: "In our system the jury decides guilt, not the sentence."
itens.ok: she needs it or the argument changes meaning
itens.porque: She needs it: in her jurisdiction the two may travel together, and without this she hears a different argument.

itens.t: "The court was built in 1942."
itens.ok: interesting, and it costs you time
itens.porque: Interesting, and it spends time you do not have.

itens.t: "We are assigned to the case -- the family does not choose us."
itens.ok: she needs it or the argument changes meaning
itens.porque: She needs it, or she will assume a retained lawyer and a choice of strategy that did not exist.

itens.t: "I have been doing jury work for eleven years."
itens.ok: it belongs later, if she asks
itens.porque: Later, if she asks. It is credentials, not the case.

itens.t: "The statement was taken eleven days after the night."
itens.ok: she needs it or the argument changes meaning
itens.porque: She needs it — the objection she is about to raise depends on it.

itens.t: "Our caseload is roughly two hundred a year."
itens.ok: it belongs later, if she asks
itens.porque: Later. It describes the office, not the argument.

nota.titulo: The middle column is the expensive one
nota.texto:
Nothing in it is false, and none of it is useless in a longer conversation. In three minutes it is what pushes the argument off the end.

The third column is different: it is what she may well ask for, and answering it then is fine. What you cannot do is spend the three minutes on it before she has.

sec4.titulo: When the objection cuts both ways
abertura: She will make one objection of substance: if the delay explains the inconsistencies, it explains them for both sides -- so why does it help you?
Mark the two responses that answer it without starting again.

itens.t: "That is fair -- it does cut both ways. The difference is who had to prove something that night."
itens.porque: Concede in four words, then give her the piece she is missing.

itens.t: "Let me go back to the beginning so the sequence is clear."
itens.porque: A restart dressed as clarity. She asked one question; this answers a different, longer one.

itens.t: "It does, and that is exactly why the burden matters here."
itens.porque: The objection is granted and turned into your own point — the strongest answer available.

itens.t: "I disagree -- the delay only affects one side."
itens.porque: It is not true, and she knows it is not. Denying a correct objection costs more than the objection did.

itens.t: "That is a different question from the one I was answering."
itens.porque: It may be accurate, and it sounds like a dodge. Say what you grant first, then draw the distinction.

sec4.rationale: The objection is correct, and denying it costs more than granting it. What answers it is the asymmetry she does not know about yet -- who carries the burden.

nota.titulo: Going back to the beginning is the expensive mistake
nota.texto:
It feels like clarity and it is a restart: three minutes become six, and she stops listening somewhere in the second one.

The move that works is to grant the objection in four words and then say the one thing she does not have. She is a lawyer — she will do the rest herself.

abertura: Complete each one so that she gets the consequence, not only the fact.

nota.titulo: Every wrong ending stops at the fact
nota.texto:
They are all true and none of them tells her what to do with it. Which is unusual, I know is even friendly — and it leaves her holding a fact with no consequence attached.

She is not slow. She simply does not have the system in her head, and assembling it is your job in these three minutes.

abertura: Complete the opening. Every gap is one of the six expressions from activity 2.

nota.titulo: This is the only thing you will write in class
nota.texto:
At stage 5 you write the opening sentence — one sentence, before you speak. Everything else in the lesson is spoken.

It is also the first sample of your written English in this cycle. The profile records writing as indeterminate; one sentence is enough to stop it being that.
